mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% year-over-year signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive or unchanged in periods of CPIAUCSL YoY > 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% signals a tightening labor market, which can lead to wage inflation and subsequently higher interest rates, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain positive or unchanged when UNRATE is below 4%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) signals strong consumer demand, which is a positive indicator for corporate earnings and thus leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative or unchanged in periods of increasing RSAFS.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a weakening supply side of the economy, which can lead to lower corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain positive or unchanged in periods of decreasing INDPRO.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 6% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) decrease, it signals a weakening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive or unchanged when UNRATE > 6% and PAYEMS decreases.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is increasing, it signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain positive or unchanged when FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL is increasing.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) signals strong demand in the housing market, which is a positive indicator for economic growth and thus leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative or unchanged in periods of sustained HOUST increases.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) is decreasing and real GDP (GDPC1) is below its 12-month moving average, it signals a weakening supply side and overall economic contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive or unchanged when INDPRO is decreasing and GDPC1 is below its 12-month moving average.
